Paragraph: O best of the Kuru dynasty, without sacrifice one can never live happily on this planet or in this life: what then of the next?
Situation/Problem_Faced: Expecting happiness and well-being while operating purely out of selfish indulgence without contribution or sacrifice.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states: 'O best of the Kuru dynasty, without sacrifice one can never live happily on this planet or in this life: what then of the next?'
Outcome/Resolution: Recognizing that sacrificial living is essential for peace in the present life and for ultimate spiritual progress.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Necessity of Contribution: Understanding that personal happiness depends on contributing to something greater than oneself
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Interconnected Well-Being: Realizing that isolationist self-centeredness leads to psychological misery
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Long-Term Satisfaction: Building lasting happiness through selflessness rather than temporary indulgence

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Nayamloko 'sty ayajnasya (This world provides no happiness for one who does not practice sacrifice)
Kuto 'nyah (What possibility is there for happiness in the next life/future state?)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Living without offering sacrifice leads to misery in this world and blocks elevation to higher spiritual states.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Egoistic living void of service fosters chronic dissatisfaction; active sacrifice is fundamental to mental health.
